output.title: Chaotic Typokinetic Text Layers - Abstract Overlapping Patterns

prompts.prompt: Create a 'typokinetics' preset that generates a chaotic, layered text composition where multiple text layers overlap and intersect like a glitched video editing timeline. Think of it as if someone duplicated text layers dozens of times in After Effects, each with slightly different positions and timings. The text should create abstract patterns through repetition and overlap, becoming intentionally unreadable as an artistic effect. Each text layer should have staggered entry animations - some sliding in from edges, others fading up, creating a cascading waterfall of text. Use rotation transforms on different layers (ranging from -45deg to 45deg) to create angular intersections. Apply varying opacity levels (30% to 100%) to create depth through transparency. The animation should feel like a kinetic typography piece that's been corrupted or remixed, with text constantly in motion through subtle drift animations after entry.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: Use BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden' as container. Create 15-20 TextAtom components, each with 'absolute' positioning and random placement using Tailwind classes like 'top-1/4 left-1/3', 'top-1/2 -left-10', 'bottom-0 right-1/4'. Apply transform classes with custom rotate values. Animation: Use generic effects with opacity and transform keyframes. Entry animations: 0.3-0.8s duration with staggered delays (index * 0.05s). Continuous drift: translateX/Y animations over 10-20s with ease-in-out. Mix font sizes using 'text-2xl' through 'text-8xl'. Blend modes: Use 'mix-blend-screen' or 'mix-blend-overlay' on alternating layers. Performance: Apply 'will-change-transform' to animated elements. Consider using repeatChildrenProps to generate multiple instances efficiently. Timing: All animations relative to parent, use fitDurationTo: 'children' to match longest animation.

prompts.prompt: Design a 'typokinetics' preset inspired by analog video feedback loops and CRT monitor interference. Imagine pointing a camera at its own monitor - the text should replicate and distort infinitely. Create a recursive visual where the same text appears at multiple scales, creating a tunnel effect of diminishing repetitions. Apply chromatic aberration by splitting text into RGB channels with slight offsets. Add scan line effects using CSS gradients. The text should pulse and flicker like unstable video signal, with occasional 'glitch' moments where all layers briefly align before scattering again. This creates an abstract pattern that's both hypnotic and disorienting, perfect for experimental title sequences.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full bg-black' container. Create nested BaseLayouts for depth, each scaled down by 0.8x. Use TextAtom with duplicate RGB layers - red channel: 'translate-x-1', blue: '-translate-x-1', green: base position. Apply 'mix-blend-screen' for color addition. Scanlines: Add overlay div with 'absolute inset-0 pointer-events-none' and repeating linear gradient background. Effects: Pulse effect using scale (0.98-1.02) over 2s. Flicker using opacity keyframes (0.8-1.0) at 100ms intervals. Glitch moments: Every 3s, all transforms reset to 0 for 200ms using spring easing. Use internal effect presets for reusable glitch and pulse effects. Caption integration: If using caption data, apply word-level timing to create cascading reveals within each layer.

prompts.prompt: Develop a 'typokinetics' preset that mimics a typographic particle system explosion. Text fragments should burst from a central point and scatter chaotically across the screen, like shrapnel from a typography bomb. Each word or letter becomes a particle with its own physics-inspired trajectory. Start with text condensed at the center, then explode outward with varying velocities and directions. Add rotation momentum to each particle. As they spread, apply motion blur through CSS filters. The overlapping trajectories create abstract line patterns, like light painting with text. Include a 'gravity' effect where particles eventually drift downward and fade out, creating a constantly regenerating cycle.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout 'relative w-full h-full flex items-center justify-center'. Generate particles using caption data words or split text into characters. Each particle: TextAtom with 'absolute' positioning starting at 'top-1/2 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2'. Animation: Use generic effects with complex keyframe arrays. Explosion: translateX/Y with randomized values (-200px to 200px), rotate (0-720deg), scale (1 to 0.5). Duration: 2-4s with cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55) for explosive feel. Motion blur: Apply 'blur(2px)' during peak velocity, reduce to 0 at rest. Gravity: Additional translateY animation adding 100-200px over time. Opacity: Fade from 1 to 0 in final 20% of animation. Use helper functions to calculate random trajectories. Consider waveform effects if audio-reactive explosion timing is desired.

prompts.prompt: Create a 'typokinetics' preset that simulates broken LCD screen aesthetics with text. Imagine a damaged display where text pixels are stuck, bleeding, or ghosting. Text should appear fragmented and misaligned, with sections randomly offsetting horizontally like corrupted scan lines. Add digital noise patterns using rapidly changing characters or Unicode glyphs overlaid on main text. Include 'dead pixel' zones where text suddenly cuts off or appears inverted. The overall effect should feel like viewing text through a malfunctioning digital display, creating beautiful chaos from technical failure.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full bg-gray-900'. Create horizontal strips using 'flex flex-col'. Each strip: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full overflow-hidden' containing TextAtom. Corruption effects: Random translateX offsets (-20px to 20px) per strip. Use clip-path to create 'dead zones': 'polygon(0 0, 80% 0, 85% 100%, 0 100%)'. Digital noise: Overlay TextAtom with rapidly changing content using setInterval in presetExecution. Apply 'mix-blend-difference' for inversion effect. Ghosting: Duplicate text layers with 'opacity-20' and slight transform offsets. Animation: Glitch transforms that jump between values without transition (0ms duration). Use internal effects for reusable corruption patterns. Performance: Limit rapid updates to visible viewport area.

prompts.prompt: Design a 'typokinetics' preset inspired by generative art and mathematical chaos theory. Text elements should follow algorithmic patterns like Perlin noise or sine wave functions, creating organic, flowing movements. Multiple text layers move in coordinated but offset patterns, like a murmuration of typographic birds. The overlapping paths create moiré patterns and interference effects. Text size and opacity should oscillate based on mathematical functions. The result is an ever-changing abstract pattern that's mesmerizing and unpredictable, perfect for ambient or artistic contexts.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout 'relative w-full h-full'. Generate 20-30 TextAtom instances using repeatChildrenProps. Position using calculated values: 'top-[calc(50%+sin(index)*40%)] left-[calc(50%+cos(index)*40%)]'. Movement: Use generic effects with complex keyframe animations. Path calculation: Helper function using sine/cosine for circular/elliptical motion. Animation values: translateX: Math.sin(time + index * 0.5) * 100, translateY: Math.cos(time + index * 0.3) * 100. Opacity oscillation: 0.3 + Math.sin(time * 2) * 0.7. Font size variation: Use calc() with CSS custom properties for dynamic sizing. Duration: 10-20s loops with ease-in-out. Consider using audio analysis for frequency-based parameter modulation. Blend modes: Alternate between 'mix-blend-multiply' and 'mix-blend-screen' for visual complexity.

prompts.prompt: Build a 'typokinetics' preset that creates a typographic kaleidoscope effect. Text should be mirrored and rotated around multiple axes, creating symmetrical patterns that constantly shift and reform. Like looking through a kaleidoscope, the same text creates entirely new abstract patterns through reflection and rotation. Include a slow rotation of the entire composition while individual segments also rotate independently. The overlapping, symmetrical chaos should create mandala-like patterns from simple text input, becoming completely abstract and unreadable.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout 'relative w-full h-full flex items-center justify-center'. Create 8 segments (45deg each) using absolute positioned BaseLayouts with 'origin-center'. Each segment: Apply rotation 'rotate-[45deg]', 'rotate-[90deg]', etc. Mirror alternating segments using 'scale-x-[-1]'. TextAtom in each with identical content but different animation phases. Animation: Container rotation using continuous rotate effect (0-360deg) over 20s linear. Individual segments: Scale breathing (0.8-1.2), opacity pulse (0.5-1). Use transform-origin manipulation for complex pivot points. Clipping: Use clip-path for triangular segments: 'polygon(50% 50%, 100% 0%, 100% 100%)'. Effects: Add blur(1px) during motion, clear when still. Performance: Use transform3d for GPU acceleration. Consider sub-presets for segment generation.

prompts.prompt: Create a 'typokinetics' preset that mimics datamoshing and compression artifacts in typography. Text should appear to melt and smear across the screen like corrupted video frames, leaving trails and ghosted impressions. Implement pixel sorting effects where parts of text stretch horizontally. Include blocky, JPEG-like compression artifacts using CSS filters and transforms. The animation should feel like text is being processed through multiple generations of lossy compression, creating abstract patterns from the degradation.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout 'relative w-full h-full bg-black overflow-hidden'. Multiple TextAtom layers with different degradation levels. Datamosh effect: Use scaleX with values up to 20 while maintaining original height. Apply 'transform-origin-left' for directional stretching. Trails: Clone text with 'absolute' positioning, apply motion blur and reduce opacity over time. Compression artifacts: Use CSS filter contrast(200%) brightness(150%) followed by blur(1px). Pixelation: Apply image-rendering: pixelated to scaled-down-then-up text. Animation: Smear effect using translateX with steps() easing for choppy movement. Ghost frames: Keep previous positions visible with decreasing opacity (0.1 steps). Use internal effects for artifact generation. Performance: Limit trail instances to 5-10 maximum.

prompts.prompt: Develop a 'typokinetics' preset inspired by liquid and fluid dynamics. Text should flow and morph like viscous liquid, pooling and separating organically. Characters should appear to have surface tension, attracting and repelling each other. Create ripple effects when new text enters, disturbing the existing text 'surface'. Use turbulence-like distortions with varying intensities across the composition. The overlapping liquid text creates abstract, ever-changing patterns like oil on water.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout 'relative w-full h-full'. Use SVG filters for liquid effects: feTurbulence and feDisplacementMap. TextAtom with filter references. Morphing: CSS filters + transform skew variations. Animation: Turbulence baseFrequency animation (0.01-0.05) over 3s. Ripple: Scale transform from center point (0.8-1.2) with spring easing. Surface tension: Calculate distances between text elements, apply attraction/repulsion forces via translateX/Y. Viscosity: Use cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55) for elastic movement. Blend modes: 'mix-blend-soft-light' for ethereal overlap. Performance: Limit SVG filter complexity, use CSS transforms for main animation. Consider using Lottie animations for complex liquid morphing if available.

prompts.prompt: Design a 'typokinetics' preset that creates a typographic storm system. Text should swirl and spiral like a tornado, with characters caught in violent circular winds. Multiple vortices of different sizes create chaotic interactions. Add perspective transforms to create depth, with text appearing to move toward and away from the viewer. Include occasional 'lightning' effects where all text briefly aligns before scattering again. The overall effect should feel like being inside a hurricane of letters and words.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout 'relative w-full h-full perspective-[1000px]'. Create vortex centers using absolute positioned containers. Spiral motion: Combine rotateZ (0-1440deg) with translateX/Y in circular pattern. Use transform3d for depth: translateZ(-500px to 500px). Each TextAtom follows orbital path with varying radius (50px-300px). Wind effect: Add turbulence using random translateX/Y offsets every 100ms. Lightning moments: All transforms reset to 0 for 100ms with flash effect (brightness(200%)). Animation timing: Vary speeds based on distance from vortex center (2s-8s). Easing: Use cubic-bezier for natural acceleration/deceleration. Opacity based on Z-depth (further = more transparent). Performance: Limit to 30-40 text elements maximum. Use will-change: transform.

prompts.prompt: Create a 'typokinetics' preset that generates ASCII art chaos. Convert text into ASCII characters that constantly shift and rearrange, creating abstract patterns from character density. Use monospace fonts to maintain grid alignment while characters randomly swap positions. Create waves of character replacement that ripple across the screen. Include sections where text becomes pure ASCII noise (random symbols) before reforming. The effect should look like a terminal window having a beautiful breakdown, where text meaning dissolves into pure visual texture.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout 'relative w-full h-full bg-black text-green-400 font-mono'. Grid system using CSS grid or flex-wrap. Each character: Individual span or TextAtom with fixed width. Character pool: Array of ASCII characters for substitution. Animation: Character swap using content replacement or opacity transitions between layers. Wave effect: Delay animations based on grid position (row * 50ms + col * 50ms). Density patterns: Vary character based on brightness needs (. for light, # for dark). Glitch: Randomly inject Unicode box-drawing characters. Use helper functions for ASCII conversion and wave calculations. Performance: Batch DOM updates, use requestAnimationFrame for smooth transitions. Consider caption data for maintaining some readable anchors within the chaos.
